adverse_media.status: Administration ongoing on the available registry evidence.
adverse_media.summary: The screened company entered administration. The registry continues to record In Administration; filing history includes a progress report filed 10 October 2026 and extension notice filed 16 September 2026. Insolvency is not itself proof of fraud.

adverse_media.status: Undertaking accepted 2 June 2026; effective 23 June 2026. Not a criminal conviction or an OFAC/UK/EU financial-sanctions designation.
adverse_media.summary: The Insolvency Service announced an accepted undertaking disqualifying Lex Greensill for nine years, effective 23 June 2026. It expressly identifies Greensill Capital (UK) Limited: he caused or allowed it to apply $440 million received in November 2020 other than to redeem the Credit Suisse fund’s notes. Transactions removed protections without required written consents. The undertaking ended the proceedings; facts were not disputed for disqualification purposes only. Amount reported by the Insolvency Service as of 4 June 2026.

adverse_media.status: Publication-meaning judgment; final disposition of the underlying defamation litigation not verified.
adverse_media.summary: The screened company was a claimant in Greensill Capital (UK) Ltd v Reuters [2020] EWHC 1325 (QB). The court determined the meaning of a publication concerning allegedly false information about Scottish Government approval of a guarantee. This was a preliminary meaning judgment, not proof that the company knowingly issued false information or committed market abuse.
adverse_media.category: Civil litigation / alleged misleading investor information

adverse_media.status: Dismissal with prejudice ordered 2 August 2022 following settlement; allegations not adjudicated in this order.
adverse_media.summary: Bluestone Resources and associated plaintiffs sued Greensill Capital (UK) Limited and individuals. The court record confirms settlement-related proceedings and voluntary dismissal of all claims against all defendants with prejudice. The dismissal is not a judicial finding that fraud occurred.

adverse_media.status: Claims against the SoftBank defendants dismissed. This is not a fraud conviction against the screened company.
adverse_media.summary: Credit Suisse v SoftBank concerned notes originated and administered by the screened company. The court’s adverse transaction-at-undervalue and creditor-prejudice findings concerned transactions entered into by Greensill Limited, a distinct vehicle. Included only because the judgment expressly links the screened company to the note programme; those findings must not be recast as a criminal judgment against it.

output.risk_rationale: High risk as of 21 October 2026: the exact UK operating entity remains in administration, and the Insolvency Service’s June 2026 enforcement outcome directly links its handling of funds and removal of creditor protections to the nine-year disqualification of its former director and registered PSC, Lex Greensill. Historical litigation adds reputational risk but must be read with its outcomes: the Bluestone case was dismissed with prejudice after settlement, the Reuters judgment determined publication meaning rather than proving fraud, and the SoftBank case involved a separate Greensill vehicle and was dismissed against SoftBank. The PSC’s former government role warrants enhanced PEP review. Sanctions results and complete beneficial ownership remain unresolved, so this screen does not support onboarding clearance. Sources: https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/08126173; https://www.gov.uk/government/news/lex-greensill-to-be-disqualified-from-acting-as-a-company-director-in-the-uk-for-nine-years; https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm5802/cmselect/cmpubadm/59/5905.htm
